status: research-only protocol frozen before C21 scan; no runtime or matches
hypothesis: A public active two-square ban gives a one-tempo safe approach to the banned square. A disclosed stronger defender cannot capture there immediately; with an aligned known Bomb/possible Flag behind that square, one Miner may force a breakthrough before the displaced defender recovers.
primary_gate: Enemy shuttle count>=5, last_to contains a disclosed rank0..6, last_from is empty. Count legal own quiet moves into last_from whose actor would otherwise be killed by that defender. No private enemy rank read.
strict_breach_gate: Own actor is Miner. Along a straight line D(defender), A(banned square), B(known enemy Bomb), F(enemy unmoved undisclosed possible Flag or disclosed Flag), each consecutive pair adjacent. Own Miner can legally move into A. Branch checking is required before any win claim; unknown F gives only a conditional objective.
additional_diagnostic: Count own decisions and selected reversals when own shuttle reaches5; no generic repetition penalty or safety claim.
proof_if_coverage: Exact legal public fixture and all legal known-enemy replies; consider other-unit resets, hidden potential capturers, own Flag counter-wins and terminal no-move rules. A ban is only temporary, never permanent immunity.
prior_distinction: Recurrence escape rewards fresh comparable continuations; target assignment diversifies disclosed objectives; local exchanges extends captures. This tests public legal response restrictions before a quiet approach, not depth, score coefficients or target uniqueness.
source_basis: Current threat and flag_threats are explicitly conservative about two-squares. Mission escorts clear a recapturer; this motif temporarily forbids its capture without clearing it.
research_basis: Allis/van den Herik/Huntjens1993 threat-space search, official AAAI FS93-02-001, motivates branching urgent responses in a short forcing line; it supplies no Stratego strength guarantee.
